findings.text: The first paragraph says clearly what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. A newcomer can say what this is within seconds.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The one section meant to show Athena's main promise (traceable models, verdict and cost) is broken and shows an error message near the top of the page. A newcomer gets no evidence for the claim that made them interested.
findings.source: Heading "Check it on a real job": "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The page is at Athena's address, but almost all of it is a detailed study of a different project, firstmate. The ledes explain that the study is a demonstration, but a newcomer looking for Athena has to read past several thousand words about firstmate's states and transitions.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and the lede "This page is that study of firstmate."

findings.text: Next steps are concrete: prerequisites, a clone command, ./setup.sh and a first command to try. The lede links straight to this section, so the reader knows what to do next.
findings.source: Heading "Next steps": "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link is for the site owner, not a newcomer. It sits in the header and may confuse a first-time reader about whether they are expected to decide something.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The firstmate study is careful, and every statement links to cited lines, which supports Athena's traceability claim. But it is long, repeats itself (for example, "in scope" and "red" are defined word for word in both "Words used first" and the Glossary), and is written for someone checking firstmate, not for someone weighing Athena.
This is internal build detail that means nothing to a newcomer, and it does not say which repository that folder is in.
findings.source: Heading "About this page": "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
